ai.description: *Herpetoreas xenura* is a slender, 50–60 cm snake with a dark brown body and pale lateral stripes. It is distinguished by a uniquely flattened, paddle-like tail and keeled dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Herpetoreas xenura* is uniquely identified by its extremely long, slender, and tapering tail, which is significantly longer relative to its body than in other keelbacks.
ai.habitat: *Herpetoreas xenura* inhabits high-altitude temperate forests and moist grassy clearings in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 2,000 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Strange-tailed Keelback is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by tightly coiling its distinctively flattened, spade-like tail when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Herpetoreas xenura* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Herpetoreas xenura* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of the Western Himalayas in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, typically occurring between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
